feats.name: Keen Mind
feats.desc: You gain the following benefits. | Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. | Lore Knowledge. Choose one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion. If you lack proficiency in the chosen skill, you gain proficiency in it, and if you already have proficiency in it, you gain Expertise in it. | Quick Study. You can take the Study action as a Bonus Action.

magicItems.name: Quaal's Feather Token
magicItems.desc: You can take a Magic action to touch the token to a boat or ship. For the next 24 hours, the vessel can’t be moved by any means. Touching the token to the vessel again ends the effect. When the effect ends, the token disappears.
magicItems._baseDesc: You can take a Magic action to touch the token to a boat or ship. For the next 24 hours, the vessel can’t be moved by any means. Touching the token to the vessel again ends the effect. When the effect ends, the token disappears.

magicItems.name: Orb of Direction
magicItems.desc: This orb can be used as an Arcane Focus. As a Magic action while holding this orb, I can determine which way is magnetic north. Nothing happens if the orb is used in a location that has no magnetic north.

magicItems.name: Ring of Silence
magicItems.desc: While wearing this ring, you cannot speak, utter sounds with your voice, or cast spells with verbal components.

magicItems.name: Thomas's Dimensional Trousers
magicItems.desc:
This flashy set of pants has four pockets that each lead to a special, extradimensional space. Each pocket is six inches wide at the mouth and can hold up to 20 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 2 cubic feet. The pants always weigh 1 pound, regardless of their contents.

Placing an object in one of the pants' pockets follows the normal rules for interacting with objects. Retrieving an item from the pants requires an action as your hand rummages around inside for a few moments before finding the item it's looking for.

If the pants are overloaded, pierced, or torn, they rupture and tear, scattering their contents in a 300-foot radius around you. Casting the *mending* spell on the pants daily for 30 days restores the pants' connection to the extradimensional spaces. If one or more pockets are turned inside out, their contents spill forth, unharmed, but the pocket must be put right before it can be used again. Breathing creatures inside the pocket can survive up to a number of minutes equal to 10 divided by the number of creatures (minimum 1 minute), after which time they begin to suffocate.

Placing the pants inside an extradimensional space created by a bag of holding, portable hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

magicItems.name: Potion of Resistance
magicItems.desc: When you drink this potion, you have Resistance to one type of damage for 1 hour. The DM chooses the type or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table.
magicItems._baseDesc: When you drink this potion, you have Resistance to one type of damage for 1 hour. The DM chooses the type or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table.

magicItems.name: Focus Circlet
magicItems.desc: While wearing this silver circlet, you gain a bonus to Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell you cast equal to the spell's level, up to a maximum of +3.

magicItems.name: Amulet of Health
magicItems.desc: My Constitution score is 19 while I'm wearing this amulet, provided that my Constitution is not already 19 or higher.

magicItems.name: Devotee's Sacrificial Blade
magicItems.desc:
When you hit a creature with an attack using this dagger, it takes damage from the attack as if it were hit from the beam of an *eldritch blast* spell you cast, using the spell's damage die and other effects associated with the spell. If you're not holding the dagger at the start of your turn, you can choose to have it magically appear in an open hand (no action required); the dagger must be on the same plane of existence as you.

*Blood for the Old Ones.* While holding the dagger, you can use an action to plunge it into your chest. When you do, you take 10 psychic damage, which can't be reduced in any way, and you can choose up to four creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you. Each chosen creature must then make an Intelligence saving throw, using your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d10 psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Psychic damage from this property ignores temporary hit points (including yours). Once a creature has taken damage from this effect, it has advantage on the saving throw against it for 24 hours. If your hit points are reduced to 0 as a result of using this property, each affected creature makes the saving throw with disadvantage; you automatically suffer 1 failed death saving throw for each time you drop to 0 hit points in this way after the first, resetting daily at dawn.

*"Your contribution to the tithe is greatly appreciated."*

magicItems.name: Mage's Manacle
magicItems.desc:
As a Magic action while wearing this bracelet, you can target a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the Grappled or Incapacitated condition. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or become magically bound to you by a spectral chain and manacle that spring from the bracelet.

While bound in this way, the creature has the Restrained condition. When you move, the creature moves with you.

A creature remains bound for 8 hours or until you release it (no action required). If the manacle takes damage from a Disintegrate spell, it is destroyed; nothing else can break or harm it. Once the manacle has bound a creature, it can't be used again this way until the next dawn.

magicItems.name: Workshop Wrecker
magicItems.desc:
When this 3-inch-diameter metal ball is activated as a Magic action, it moves at a rapid speed, bouncing off walls and defying any attempts to capture it. The ball remains active for 1 minute or until you deactivate it by using a command word while within 30 feet of it (no action required). Once the ball is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

When you activate the ball and at the beginning of each of your turns while the ball is active, each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Bludgeoning damage on a failed save. The save DC and amount of damage dealt depend on the approximate size of the area in which the ball is active, as shown on the following table.

A nonmagical object that isn't being worn or carried also takes the damage if it is in the area. In confined areas larger than a 100-foot Cube, the amount of damage caused by the ball is negligible. If the ball is activated in an unconfined area, it flies off in a random direction at a rate of 300 feet per round.

***Area | Save DC | Bludgeoning Damage***
15-foot Cube | 18 | 6d6+5
30-foot Cube | 17 | 4d6+4
50-foot Cube | 15 | 2d6+2
100-foot Cube | 14 | 1d6+1

grantedResources.name: Workshop Wrecker
grantedResources.desc: Activate the bouncing ball for up to 1 minute of area Bludgeoning damage — see item description for the size/DC/damage table.

magicItems.name: Iron Flask
magicItems.desc:
While holding this brass-stoppered iron flask, you can take a Magic action to target a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. If the flask is empty and the target is native to a plane of existence other than the one you're on, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be trapped in the flask. If the target has been trapped by the flask before, it has Advantage on the save. Once trapped, a creature remains in the flask until released. The flask can hold only one creature at a time. A creature trapped in the flask doesn't age and doesn't need to breathe, eat, or drink.

You can take a Magic action to remove the flask's stopper and release the creature in the flask. The creature then obeys your commands for 1 hour, understanding those commands even if it doesn't know the language in which the commands are given. If you issue no commands or give the creature a command that is likely to result in its death or imprisonment, it defends itself but otherwise takes no actions. At the end of the duration, the creature acts in accordance with its normal disposition and alignment.

An *Identify* spell reveals if the flask contains a creature, but the only way to determine the type of creature is to open the flask. A newly discovered Iron Flask might already contain a creature chosen by the DM or determined randomly by rolling on the following table (see the *Monster Manual* for the creature's stat block).

magicItems.name: Crystal Ball of Ominous Portent
magicItems.desc:
Black-and-scarlet clouds of ominous magic swirl inside this crystal orb. While touching the orb, you can cast Hex or Scrying (save DC 17) with it.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 60 feet succeeds on a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to turn the roll into a 1. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

grantedResources.name: Ominous Portent
grantedResources.desc: Turn a creature's successful D20 Test into a 1.

magicItems._baseDesc:
A magical Tiny vessel that serves as a spellcasting focus for warlock spells. Its AC equals the wielder's spell save DC ({{VESSEL_AC}}), and it has Hit Points equal to their warlock level + their Proficiency Bonus ({{VESSEL_HP}}). If destroyed or lost, it can be replaced with a 1-hour ceremony during a rest. Its exact form depends on the warlock's Genie Kind — a brass bottle, a woven basket, a jeweled flask, a shattered flagon, or similar.

Bottled Respite: the vessel's extradimensional space is a 20-ft-radius, 20-ft-high cylinder. Items left inside remain there until taken out or the vessel is destroyed — functionally the same as a Bag of Holding for storage purposes.

magicItems.name: The King in Yellow
magicItems.desc:
A slim play-script bound in cloth the color of old fever, no author credited. Its first act is dull. No one has ever left its second act unread.

**Attunement.** You can't choose to end attunement to this book. It ends only if the book is destroyed. Attuning to this book doesn't count against the number of magic items you can be attuned to.

**Act I: The Stranger.** When you attune to this book, choose one of the following. You have no memory of how you came by it.
- _**Spell.**_ You learn one spell of your choice from any class's spell list. You always have it prepared, and you can cast it once without a spell slot, regaining this ability when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose when you attune).
- _**Feat.**_ You gain one Origin feat of your choice.

**Spell Granted:** *Plant Growth*

**Act II: The Yellow Sign.** When you finish a Long Rest without having read Act II, make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw, which increases by 1 for each success. On a failure, you've read it. Once you have, you bear *the Yellow Sign*, visible only to those who have read the play, and you gain the following properties.

_**Carcosa's Favor.**_ You have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition, and you gain Proficiency and Expertise in Charisma (Performance).

_**I Wear No Mask.**_ As a Bonus Action, you gain Truesight out to 30 feet for 1 minute. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

_**Have You Found the Yellow Sign?**_ As a Magic action, you ask the question of one creature you can see within 60 feet that can hear you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (your spell save DC, or DC 15 if you lack the Spellcasting feature) or have the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions until the end of its next turn, at which point it must repeat the save. If it fails the second save, it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The effect ends on the target if it takes damage or someone within 5 feet of it takes an action to shake it free. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

_**An Audience with the King.**_ When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, or in another moment of desperate struggle (DM's discretion), you can beg an audience with the King in Yellow (no action required). For an instant you stand in Carcosa, and the King grants you one of the following:
- **Rise.** You regain all your Hit Points, and all conditions on you end.
- **Unmask.** Each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (same DC as above) or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute, during which its Speed is 0. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
- **Command.** You immediately cast any spell of level 6 or lower without expending a spell slot or needing components.

**The King's Favour.** Roll on the Carcosan Madness table; the effect lasts until ended by *Greater Restoration* or *Remove Curse*. The King also asks a favor of you, chosen by the DM. You can't use this property again until you've granted it.

_**Curse: Carcosan Madness.**_ Whenever you finish a Long Rest, roll a d20. On a 1, roll on the Carcosan Madness table; the effect lasts until your next Long Rest. On a 20, you dream of twin suns and gain Heroic Inspiration.

| **d10** | Carcosan Madness                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| :-----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|  **1**  | **Lost Carcosa.** Sometimes you forget which world is the real one. Whenever you roll Initiative, roll a d6. On a 1, you have the Incapacitated condition until the end of your first turn.                                                                                                                             |
|  **2**  | **The Black Stars.** You keep searching a sky that isn't there, even indoors. You have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, but you always know which way is north and how long it is until the next dawn or dusk.                                                                            |
|  **3**  | **Cassilda's Song.** You can't stop humming the song, and its lines slip into your speech. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and any creature that has read the play knows your location while it is within 120 feet of you.                                                                         |
|  **4**  | **The Pallid Mask.** Your face doesn't feel like your own, and you keep touching it. You have Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception and Persuasion) checks, but you can cast *Disguise Self* at will, without a spell slot.                                                                                               |
|  **5**  | **The Repairer of Reputations.** You keep a ledger of every slight against you, and your allies are in it. You can't benefit from the Help action, and you won't let anyone else carry your belongings.                                                                                                                 |
|  **6**  | **The Hyades.** Distant voices sing from a sky that isn't there, drowning out the room around you. You have Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration, but you can't have the Deafened condition.                                                                                            |
|  **7**  | **Lake of Hali.** Your limbs feel waterlogged and your lungs feel wet. Your Speed is reduced by 10 feet, but you can breathe water and you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.                                                                                                                                       |
|  **8**  | **Yhtill's Spires.** You glimpse impossible towers behind the horizon, and heights pull at you. You have Disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) checks, and whenever you're within 10 feet of a drop of 20 feet or more, you must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or move toward its edge using all your movement. |
|  **9**  | **The Watchman.** A puffy, pale-faced figure watches you from just too far away to reach. You sleep poorly and regain only half your spent Hit Dice on a Long Rest, but you can't be Surprised.                                                                                                                         |
| **10**  | **Not Upon Us, O King.** Despair settles on you, and nothing feels like it will help. You can't gain Heroic Inspiration, and you have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.                                                                                                                                              |
